name: Timothy's father (Greek, unnamed)
title: The Greek Father
summary: Timothy's father was a Greek (gentile) who married the Jewish woman Eunice. He is not named in the Bible, but his Greek background explains why Timothy was not circumcised as a child, which Paul later arranged before the missionary journeys.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as the Greek father
keyEvents.description: Luke tells us that Timothy's mother was a believing Jewish woman, but his father was Greek. This was a mixed marriage union known in diaspora communities.

keyEvents.title: Reason for Timothy's lack of circumcision
keyEvents.description: Because his father was Greek, Timothy had not been circumcised as an infant according to Jewish custom. Paul later circumcised him out of consideration for the Jews in the area.
